text: Driftwood's engineering org now ships a dozen services a week. Before any cluster gets built, Theo and VP of Engineering Casey Lindqvist sort them into three buckets: moving to Kubernetes now, staying as-is for this phase, and explicitly deferred for a later one.

Only three services move now: catalog-api, checkout-api, and cart-api — the browse, add-to-cart, and pay path every shopper walks during the sale. If any one of those three fails under load, the sale fails. Everything else is deliberately out of scope for this phase, written down to revisit later, not quietly dropped.

The sale date isn't an arbitrary deadline — it's the forcing function that keeps this scope honest. Every decision gets judged against one question: will this hold up under the sale's real, verified traffic? That rules out database migrations, re-architecting service internals, and a service mesh for this phase.

And because these three services already run in production with real customers today, this is a migration, not a greenfield build — each one needs a validated parallel path onto Kubernetes and a real, rehearsed rollback, not a big-bang replace. Lesson 3 turns this scope into an actual target architecture.
